# LeapOfFaith Workspace Architecture

Use these as default guidance for this workspace. If a task explicitly asks for a different approach, follow the task and explain the tradeoff.

- Treat this repository as a multi-module libGDX project with three active modules:
- `core`: shared game logic and platform-agnostic code.
- `lwjgl3`: desktop launcher/backend and desktop packaging tasks.
- `teavm`: web launcher/backend and web build/serve tasks.

- Place shared gameplay code in `core/src/main/java/com/mika/leapoffaith`.
- Keep platform-specific bootstrapping in launcher modules:
- Desktop entry point: `lwjgl3/src/main/java/com/mika/leapoffaith/lwjgl3/Lwjgl3Launcher.java`.
- Web entry point: `teavm/src/main/java/com/mika/leapoffaith/teavm/TeaVMLauncher.java`.

- Keep Java compatibility at 21 when editing Gradle files.
- Add cross-platform dependencies to `core/build.gradle`.
- Add backend-specific dependencies only to the relevant launcher module (`lwjgl3` or `teavm`).

- Treat `assets/` as the canonical asset source for runtime resources.
- Do not hand-edit `assets/assets.txt`; it is generated by the `generateAssetList` task wired into `processResources`.
- Load assets by relative paths (for example `new Texture("libgdx.png")`) so both desktop and web launchers can resolve them.

- Prefer these commands for validation and run flows:
- Always use the Gradle wrapper (`./gradlew`) when suggesting build, run, or test commands.
- Desktop run: `./gradlew lwjgl3:run`
- Web run (Jetty): `./gradlew teavm:run`
- Web build only: `./gradlew teavm:build`
- Full build: `./gradlew build`
- Tests: `./gradlew test`

- Do not edit generated output under `build/` directories; change source files and Gradle scripts instead.
- Preserve existing package naming rooted at `com.mika.leapoffaith` unless a deliberate refactor is requested.
